data.name: Interval_Hint
data.value: How often repositories with auto-fetch or auto-pull are synced

data.name: Refresh_Hint
data.value: Read the status of all repositories again

data.name: Scan_Hint
data.value: Look for repositories in a folder, three levels deep

data.name: Empty_Text
data.value: Add single repositories or let RepoBoard look through a folder like {0}.

data.name: Col_AutoFetch_Hint
data.value: git fetch in the background at the interval

data.name: Col_AutoPull_Hint
data.value: After the fetch, fast-forward when it is safe

data.name: UpstreamGone_Hint
data.value: {0} no longer exists on the remote – usually after its pull request was merged

data.name: NoUpstream_Hint
data.value: Never pushed – a push sets the upstream

data.name: UpToDate_Hint
data.value: Same as {0} (as of the last fetch)

data.name: Remove_Hint
data.value: Remove from the board (the folder stays)

data.name: NewBranch_Placeholder
data.value: New branch from the current state

data.name: Tray_Open
data.comment: Menu item of the notification-area icon

data.name: Tray_PauseAutoSync
data.comment: Menu item (checked while paused) and switch in the settings

data.name: Tray_Exit
data.comment: Menu item of the notification-area icon: ends RepoBoard

data.name: Tray_HintTitle
data.comment: Notification after the window was closed for the first time

data.name: Tray_HintText
data.value: Auto-sync goes on in the notification area. Exit from the icon’s menu, or change what closing does in the settings.

data.name: Tray_ReposOther
data.comment: Tooltip of the notification-area icon. {0} = number of repositories

data.name: Tray_Behind
data.comment: Tooltip. {0} = number of repositories behind their upstream

data.name: Tray_Problems
data.comment: Tooltip. {0} = number of repositories with an error or a blocked auto-pull

data.name: Paused_Hint
data.value: Auto-sync is paused until you resume it or RepoBoard restarts. The status is still read, and every button works.

data.name: Settings_CloseToTray
data.value: Keep running in the notification area when the window is closed

data.name: Settings_Autostart
data.value: Start with Windows (in the notification area)

data.name: Settings_Notifications
data.comment: Label of the choice when Windows notifications are shown

data.name: Diff_Show_Hint
data.value: Show the changes in this file

data.name: Diff_Staged
data.comment: Label of a diff: the changes already in the index

data.name: Diff_Unstaged
data.comment: Label of a diff: the changes not yet in the index

data.name: Diff_Binary
data.value: Binary file – there is no text diff.

data.name: Diff_NestedRepository
data.value: This folder is a repository of its own – there is no diff for it here.

data.name: Diff_TooLarge
data.value: This file is larger than {0} MB – its diff is not shown.

data.name: Diff_Truncated
data.value: Only the first {0:N0} lines are shown.

data.name: Diff_NoTextChanges
data.value: No text changes – for example, only the file mode changed.

data.name: Diff_Conflict
data.value: This file has conflicts. Open it in VS Code to resolve them, then mark it as resolved.

data.name: Diff_NoNewline
data.value: No newline at end of file

data.name: Diff_StageHunk
data.comment: Button at a block of changes in the diff

data.name: Diff_UnstageHunk
data.comment: Button at a block of changes in the diff of the staged side

data.name: Diff_StageLines
data.comment: Button at a block of changes in the diff. {0} = number of selected lines

data.name: Diff_StageHunk_Hint
data.value: All changes of this hunk. To take single lines, click them at the left edge – Shift+click selects a range.

data.name: Diff_StageLines_Hint
data.value: Only the selected lines of this hunk

data.name: Diff_PickLine_Hint
data.value: Select this line – Shift+click selects a range

data.name: Worktrees_Hint
data.comment: Tooltip of the count badge in a repository's row. {0} = number of linked worktrees

data.name: Worktree_Claude
data.comment: Badge of a worktree a Claude Code session made (in .claude\worktrees)

data.name: Worktree_Claude_Hint
data.value: Made by a Claude Code session – a session may still be working in it.

data.name: Worktree_Locked
data.comment: Badge of a worktree locked with git worktree lock

data.name: Worktree_Locked_Hint
data.value: Locked with git worktree lock – it is not removed.

data.name: Worktree_Locked_Reason
data.value: Locked with git worktree lock: “{0}” – it is not removed.
data.comment: {0} = the reason given to git worktree lock

data.name: Worktree_Remove_Hint
data.value: Remove worktree … (deletes its folder; the branch stays)

data.name: Worktrees_CleanUp
data.comment: Button below a repository's worktrees that opens the clean-up dialog

data.name: Worktrees_CleanUp_Hint
data.value: Find the worktrees that look done (merged, upstream deleted, folder gone) and remove them

data.name: Worktrees_RemoveExplain
data.value: Removing deletes the worktree’s folder with git worktree remove. Branches and commits stay; git refuses a worktree with changed or new files.

data.name: Worktrees_NoDefaultBranch
data.value: origin/HEAD is not set, so merged branches can’t be recognized. “git remote set-head origin --auto” sets it.

data.name: Worktrees_Reason_FolderMissing
data.value: The folder is gone – only git’s data about it is removed.

data.name: Worktrees_ClaudeWarning
data.value: A Claude worktree is ticked: if a session still works in it, it loses its folder.

data.name: Worktrees_RemoveOther
data.comment: {0} = number of worktrees (0 or more than 1)

data.name: History_AllBranches_Hint
data.value: Show the commits of every local and remote branch, not only of the current one

data.name: History_Open_Hint
data.value: Show the commit's message, files and changes

data.name: Commit_MergeNote
data.value: Merge commit: the files and changes against its first parent – what the merge brought into the branch.

data.name: Commit_Revert_Hint
data.value: Add a new commit that undoes this one

data.name: Commit_CherryPick_Hint
data.value: Apply this commit onto {0} as a new commit

data.name: Amend_Hint
data.value: Replace the last commit with the staged changes and this message – only while it is not pushed

data.name: Operation_MergeTitle
data.comment: {0} = the merge message git prepared, e.g. Merge branch 'feature'

data.name: Operation_RebaseTitle
data.value: Rebase of {0} in progress – commit {1} of {2}: {3}
data.comment: {0} = branch being rebased, {1} = current step, {2} = number of steps, {3} = subject of the commit it stopped at

data.name: Operation_PickTitle
data.comment: {0} = Cherry-pick or Revert (Operation_…), {1} = short commit id, {2} = commit subject

data.name: Operation_Continue
data.comment: Button: go on with the stopped merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert

data.name: Operation_Continue_Hint
data.value: Commit what is staged with git’s message and go on

data.name: Operation_Skip
data.comment: Button: leave out the commit the operation stopped at

data.name: Operation_Skip_Hint
data.value: Leave out this commit and go on with the next one

data.name: Operation_Abort
data.comment: Button: end the stopped operation and go back to the state before it

data.name: Operation_Abort_Hint
data.value: End the {0} and go back to the state before it

data.name: Operation_AbortText
data.value: The repository goes back to the state before the {0}. What you resolved is lost, and these changed files may go back with it (git keeps a change of yours where it can); new files stay:

data.name: Operation_SkipText
data.value: The commit “{0}” is left out and what you resolved for it is lost. These changed files may go back:
data.comment: {0} = subject or short id of the commit

data.name: Conflict_Open
data.comment: Button: open a conflicted file in VS Code

data.name: Conflict_Open_Hint
data.value: Open in VS Code – resolve the conflict there, also in its merge editor

data.name: Conflict_Resolved
data.comment: Button: mark a conflicted file as resolved

data.name: Conflict_Resolved_Hint
data.value: Mark as resolved: stage the file as it is now

data.name: Conflict_MarkersText
data.value: git still finds conflict markers in {0}. Mark it as resolved anyway?

data.name: Conflict_DeletedByUs
data.comment: Conflict kind (git status: deleted by us)

data.name: Conflict_DeletedByThem
data.comment: Conflict kind (git status: deleted by them)

data.name: Conflict_AddedByUs
data.comment: Conflict kind (git status: added by us)

data.name: Conflict_AddedByThem
data.comment: Conflict kind (git status: added by them)

data.name: Branch_Merge
data.comment: Button: merge this branch into the current one

data.name: Branch_Rebase
data.comment: Button: rebase the current branch onto this one

data.name: Branch_Rebase_Hint
data.value: Rebase {1} onto {0} – only while its commits are not pushed

data.comment: Button: close a question without doing what it asks about, where Cancel would read as the action itself (Abort)
